# KRN-004: Kernel hardening sysctls match the baseline

- **Group:** Kernel settings
- **Severity when it fails:** low
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

kptr_restrict, dmesg_restrict, protected hardlinks, symlinks, fifos and regular files, unprivileged BPF and ptrace_scope make local privilege escalation harder by hiding kernel addresses and restricting common attack primitives.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sysctl kernel.kptr_restrict kernel.dmesg_restrict kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled kernel.yama.ptrace_scope fs.protected_hardlinks fs.protected_symlinks fs.protected_fifos fs.protected_regular
```

## How to fix it

Set the values in a /etc/sysctl.d drop-in.

## What a fix can break

ptrace_scope of 1 or more stops debuggers from attaching to processes that are not their children; strace -p and gdb need root or a set value.

Run `stackward explain KRN-004` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
